FX swaps are a tool frequently employed by the SBV, primarily to support short-term liquidity within the banking system.
This year, the central bank conducted several FX swap transactions, ranging from $1 billion to $2 billion in volume, but these were for short tenors of less than 30 days.
This FX swap marks the first time the SBV has executed such a transaction with a relatively longer tenor.

Besides, the SBV believed that the flexible FX swap instruments has helped support short-term liquidity within the system, while maintaining interest rate differentials at appropriate levels to mitigate pressure on the exchange rate.

According to analysts from the VPS Securities Company, the SBV has conducted several FX swap operations since the beginning of this year, typically with maturities ranging from three to 21 days and maximum sizes of $1 billion to $2 billion.
Extending the maturity to 182 days therefore marks a notable shift in the SBV's approach to liquidity management.
VPS's analysts said that the SBV was proactively supporting VNĐ liquidity amid rising funding demand across the banking system.

The maximum volume of dollars to be purchased by the SBV will be the amount necessary to bring each institution's foreign currency position back to a balanced state, based on data from the end of the working day immediately preceding the transaction session.
Through this mechanism, banks with qualifying dollar holdings can sell their dollars to the SBV in exchange for Vietnamese đồng at the set purchase rate.

SBV proposes to raise classification criteria for banks

HÀ NỘI - A commercial bank must have a total asset value of VNĐ500 trillion (US$18.9 billion) or more to be qualified for ranking as 'large-sized' one, starting from 2027, according to a new proposal of the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV).

Under a draft circular, which will replace Circular No. 21/2025/TT-NHNN on regulating the rating of credit institutions and foreign bank branches, the SBV proposes various changes regarding the criteria for categorising banks, as well as the assessment of liquidity and capital adequacy.
In the draft circular, the SBV proposes increasing the threshold for the large-sized bank to VNĐ500 trillion starting from the 2027 rating year.

Specifically, the SBV proposes incorporating the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) and the net stable funding ratio (NSFR) into the bank assessment and rating framework, while also adjusting the application of the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR).

The SBV also proposes a roadmap to gradually increase the scoring thresholds for both the average LCR and the NSFR, to be applied consistently across large-scale commercial banks, small-scale commercial banks, and foreign bank branches.

In addition to liquidity-related provisions, the draft circular also introduces a mechanism for determining scoring thresholds for capital-related indicators, applicable in the event that the SBV's Governor decides to implement the countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB).

Rather than relying solely on historical data, these thresholds may now be derived from the minimum or maximum limits stipulated by the SBV regarding safety ratios and operational constraints for credit institutions and foreign bank branches.

The SBV intends to implement these amendments and supplements starting from the 2027 rating year, ensuring alignment with the timeline for when commercial banks and foreign bank branches may begin opting for the early application of Circular No. 50/2026/TT-NHNN.
